purpose: Source-separated audit matrix. Wild feeding observations are descriptive and never converted directly into captive percentages, unlimited feeding, or nutrition completeness claims.

iftime_ibera_dobrogea_2012.supports: Direct evidence that wild T. g. ibera consumed reported plant taxa/parts; study reports over 95% plant matter and 25 plant species consumed.
iftime_ibera_dobrogea_2012.does_not_support: Captive diet percentages, unlimited feeding, exact portions, nutritional completeness, or safety of unobserved congeners.

mitrevichin_ibera_bulgaria_2023.supports: Direct field observations of T. g. ibera feeding on Cichorium intybus, Taraxacum sp., Medicago sp., Sedum rubens, Sedum album and Potentilla sp.
mitrevichin_ibera_bulgaria_2023.does_not_support: Quantitative captive frequency, exact portion, unlimited feeding, or inference to every species in the same genus.

slimani2006.sample_context: faecal analysis with plant availability comparison
slimani2006.supports: Direct T. g. graeca feeding ecology. Malva parviflora was among five main plant species; the five together represented about 70% of identified material. The study identified 34 plant species in the diet.
slimani2006.does_not_support: Exact Ibera evidence, Korean retail-name mapping, captive percentages, or safety of all Malva/Medicago/Astragalus species.

algeria_graeca_food_choice_2008.sample_context: 4422 plant/animal fragments from faecal pellets of 20 males, 16 females and 8 juveniles
algeria_graeca_food_choice_2008.supports: Broad wild T. graeca feeding ecology; 13 dicot and 3 monocot plant species were consumed and vegetative tissues exceeded reproductive tissues.
algeria_graeca_food_choice_2008.does_not_support: Exact Ibera evidence or safety/frequency of a Korean retail plant without a taxon-level match.

foods.audit_interpretation: Strong direct applicability for occurrence in the natural diet of T. g. ibera. It does not establish daily, unlimited, or sole-staple captive use.

direct_evidence.observation: Taraxacum reported among young leaves for which a feeding predilection was observed

foods.audit_interpretation: Repeated direct Ibera evidence at Taraxacum genus level; master identity remains genus-level, so no species-specific inference.

direct_evidence.observation: Sonchus reported among young leaves for which a feeding predilection was observed

foods.audit_interpretation: Direct Ibera evidence exists at genus level; this does not identify every Sonchus species as interchangeable.

direct_evidence.observation: Trifolium reported among young leaves for which a feeding predilection was observed

foods.audit_interpretation: Direct Ibera occurrence evidence at genus level; wild preference does not establish a captive feeding ratio.

direct_evidence.observation: Medicago reported among young leaves for which a feeding predilection was observed

related_species_evidence.observation: Medicago hispida was one of five main plant species in the diet

foods.audit_interpretation: Direct Ibera evidence is Medicago-genus level, not an exact M. sativa observation. Keep exact-species identity and feeding-frequency claims separate.

related_species_evidence.observation: Malva parviflora was a major wild diet item; about 15% of identified material in the reported dataset

foods.audit_interpretation: Useful species-level evidence exists for M. parviflora in T. g. graeca, but it must not unlock the Korean generic mallow entry until species identity is reconciled.

related_species_evidence.observation: Plantago amplexicaulis occurred in the study vegetation and was only rarely recovered as a food item in the reported dataset

foods.audit_interpretation: Do not upgrade the Plantago master entry from this study. The evidence concerns P. amplexicaulis in T. g. graeca and does not establish broad Plantago safety or preference for Ibera.
Excellent exact-Ibera genus-context evidence, but not an exact S. sarmentosum observation. Keep the Korean 돌나물 identity and feeding verdict dependent on separate exact-species evidence.

No direct T. g. ibera Morus evidence was verified in this audit pass. A 2023 Bulgaria report depicts T. hermanni feeding on mulberries, not T. graeca ibera; that observation must not be transferred across species.
No exact-Ibera leaf-feeding evidence was verified in this audit pass. Reports of fruit consumption or observations in T. hermanni are not evidence for Ficus carica leaves in T. g. ibera.
No direct Ibera field evidence verified in this pass; retain specialist/general evidence separately and do not imply a wild-Ibera observation.
